questions.question: What problem does the lakehouse architecture solve?
options: It serves warehouse and data-lake workloads from one open storage format
It removes the need for any compute
It stores data only in memory
questions.explanation: A lakehouse keeps data in an open format such as Delta Lake so BI, data engineering and ML all work on the same copy.

questions.question: Which of these lives in the Databricks-managed control plane?
options: The Spark executors running your query
The notebook UI and job scheduler
questions.explanation: The control plane holds the web application, notebooks and scheduler. Data and Spark execution live in the compute plane.

questions.question: What kind of compute does Databricks Free Edition provide?
questions.explanation: Free Edition is serverless-only and quota-limited.

questions.question: Which magic command runs a single notebook cell as SQL?
questions.explanation: %sql switches one cell to SQL regardless of the notebook's default language.

questions.question: Why connect a Git folder to GitHub at the start of the program?
options: It versions every notebook and file so your work can be reviewed and verified
It is required to create a catalog
It gives you more compute quota
questions.explanation: Git folders put notebooks and files under version control. This program verifies your repo every day.

questions.question: What is Unity Catalog's namespace for a table?
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog uses a three-level namespace: catalog, schema, then table (or view, volume, function or model).

questions.question: Which object governs non-tabular files such as CSVs, images or PDFs?
questions.explanation: Volumes are Unity Catalog securables for files, addressed as /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/...

questions.question: Which statement removes a privilege that was previously granted?
questions.explanation: REVOKE takes back a grant. DENY explicitly blocks a privilege even if it is granted elsewhere.

questions.question: Why should production jobs run as a service principal?
options: The job doesn't break or change behaviour when a person leaves or loses access
It is the only way to schedule a job
questions.explanation: A service principal is a non-human identity, so production access isn't tied to one employee's account.

questions.question: How are row filters and column masks defined in Unity Catalog?
options: As SQL functions attached to a table
As JSON files in a Volume
questions.explanation: You write a SQL UDF and attach it with SET ROW FILTER or ALTER COLUMN ... SET MASK.

questions.question: Where does Delta Lake record every committed change to a table?
questions.explanation: Each commit is a JSON entry in _delta_log, which is what makes ACID transactions and time travel possible.

questions.question: Which query reads a table as it was at an earlier version?
options: SELECT * FROM t VERSION AS OF 0
questions.explanation: VERSION AS OF (or TIMESTAMP AS OF) reads a past snapshot. DESCRIBE HISTORY lists the versions.

questions.question: Why can VACUUM with a very short retention break time travel?
options: It removes old data files that earlier versions still point to
questions.explanation: VACUUM deletes unreferenced data files older than the retention threshold, so older versions can no longer be read.

questions.question: What does Liquid Clustering replace for most tables?
questions.explanation: Liquid Clustering lays data out by clustering keys incrementally, replacing most hand-tuned partitioning and Z-ordering.

questions.question: What does MERGE INTO do in a single atomic statement?
options: Updates matched rows and inserts unmatched rows
questions.explanation: MERGE is Delta's upsert: WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE, WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT.

questions.question: What happens when you run the same COPY INTO a second time with no new files?
options: It loads zero new rows because it tracks files it already loaded
questions.explanation: COPY INTO is idempotent: files already loaded into the target are skipped.

questions.question: Which source format name is used for Auto Loader?
questions.explanation: Auto Loader is spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles") with cloudFiles.* options.

questions.question: Which streaming trigger does serverless compute support for an Auto Loader stream?
questions.explanation: Serverless supports AvailableNow (and the deprecated Once). It processes all available data and then stops.

questions.question: What does cloudFiles.schemaLocation store?
options: The inferred schema and its evolution over time
questions.explanation: Auto Loader keeps the inferred schema there so it can detect and evolve new columns across runs.

questions.question: A source database needs continuous sync into Databricks. What fits best?
questions.explanation: Managed Lakeflow Connect connectors handle incremental database and SaaS ingestion for you.

questions.question: Which medallion layer holds cleaned, deduplicated and typed data?
questions.explanation: Bronze is raw, Silver is cleaned and conformed, and Gold is business-level aggregates.

questions.question: What does broadcast(df) do in a join?
options: Sends the small DataFrame to every executor so the big side isn't shuffled
Writes the DataFrame to a Volume
Splits the DataFrame into more partitions
questions.explanation: A broadcast hash join copies the small table everywhere and avoids shuffling the large one.

questions.question: Which function gives a fast, approximate distinct count?
questions.explanation: approx_count_distinct uses HyperLogLog++ to estimate distinct counts cheaply on large data.

questions.question: When is a view a better Gold object than a table?
options: When the result must be stored for fast reads
When the definition changes often and the data is cheap to recompute
When you need to VACUUM it
questions.explanation: A view stores only the query, so changing its logic never leaves stale materialized data behind.

questions.question: What is spark.sql.shuffle.partitions set to by default on serverless compute?
questions.explanation: Open-source Spark defaults to 200, but serverless sets it to auto and lets the engine size shuffles.

questions.question: What was Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines previously called?
questions.explanation: Delta Live Tables was renamed Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines.

questions.question: What does ON VIOLATION DROP ROW do in an expectation?
options: Drops invalid rows and keeps processing
Keeps invalid rows and logs a warning
questions.explanation: DROP ROW discards failing rows and records them in the data quality metrics. FAIL UPDATE stops the update instead.

questions.question: Which object type recomputes an aggregate over its full input and keeps it up to date?
questions.explanation: Materialized views keep query results current. Streaming tables process append-only data incrementally.

questions.question: What does STREAM(products_bronze) mean in a pipeline query?
options: Read the table incrementally as a stream
Export the table to a file
Copy the table to another schema
questions.explanation: STREAM() reads only new data from the upstream table, which is what a streaming table needs.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of a declarative pipeline over hand-written ingestion and transforms?
options: The platform handles ordering, retries, dependencies and data quality enforcement for you
It only works with CSV files
It removes the need for Unity Catalog
questions.explanation: You declare the tables and rules, and the pipeline manages execution order, retries and expectations.

questions.question: What was Lakeflow Jobs previously called?
questions.explanation: Databricks Workflows was renamed Lakeflow Jobs.

questions.question: How does a notebook task read a parameter named top_n?
questions.explanation: Task parameters arrive as notebook widgets, read with dbutils.widgets.get.

questions.question: Which trigger starts a job when new files land in a location?
questions.explanation: File arrival triggers watch a storage location or Volume and start a run when new files appear.

questions.question: Why add retries to an ingestion task?
options: To recover automatically from transient failures
questions.explanation: Retries absorb transient errors such as timeouts without anyone having to re-run the job by hand.

questions.question: Why compare a job's run durations over time?
options: To catch a pipeline that is silently getting slower
questions.explanation: Run history against a baseline reveals gradual regressions before they become outages.

questions.question: What are Declarative Automation Bundles?
options: Jobs, pipelines and other resources defined as YAML and deployed with the CLI
questions.explanation: Bundles (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles) describe resources as code in databricks.yml.

questions.question: Which command checks a bundle for configuration errors without deploying it?
questions.explanation: validate catches config and permission problems before anything is deployed.

questions.question: What is a bundle target?
options: A table the bundle writes to
An environment such as dev or prod with its own overrides
questions.explanation: Targets let the same bundle deploy with different settings to dev, test and prod.

questions.question: Which command deploys a bundle to its prod target?
questions.explanation: deploy -t <target> pushes the bundle's resources to that environment.

questions.question: What should a CI pipeline typically run when a pull request merges to main?
options: Only unit tests on the laptop
questions.explanation: Automating validate and deploy on merge keeps environments in sync with reviewed code.

questions.question: On serverless compute, where do you inspect a query's execution details?
questions.explanation: The Spark UI isn't available on serverless. The query profile shows operator-level time, rows, shuffle and spill.

questions.question: What is data skew?
options: A few keys holding a disproportionate share of rows, overloading some tasks
questions.explanation: Skew makes a handful of tasks do most of the work while the rest sit idle.

questions.question: How does salting help with a skewed join key?
options: It adds a random suffix so the hot key's rows spread across partitions
questions.explanation: Salting splits one hot key into many sub-keys, with the other side replicated to match.

questions.question: What does spill mean in a query profile?
options: Data written from memory to disk because a task ran out of memory
questions.explanation: Spill slows queries down. Fixes include more memory, more partitions or reducing data before the wide operation.

questions.question: What does Predictive Optimization do for Unity Catalog managed tables?
options: Runs OPTIMIZE and VACUUM automatically when they're worthwhile
Chooses the cluster size for notebooks
questions.explanation: It schedules maintenance like OPTIMIZE and VACUUM for you based on how tables are used.

questions.question: What compute runs Databricks SQL queries and AI/BI dashboards?
questions.explanation: SQL warehouses are the compute behind the SQL Editor, dashboards, alerts and Genie.

questions.question: Which AI/BI dashboard visualization shows a single KPI number?
questions.explanation: A counter widget displays one big number, optionally against a target.

questions.question: What is AI/BI Genie?
options: Natural-language Q&A that generates SQL over governed data
questions.explanation: Genie turns business questions into SQL against the tables you curate in a Genie space.

questions.question: How do you make Genie answer more reliably?
options: Curate the space with trusted assets, instructions and sample questions
questions.explanation: Curation grounds Genie in the right tables and in how your business phrases questions.

questions.question: Whose permissions govern what a Genie user can see?
options: Genie has its own separate permission model
questions.explanation: Genie queries run under Unity Catalog governance, so users only see data they're allowed to read.

questions.question: What does mlflow.autolog() do?
options: Automatically logs parameters, metrics and models for supported libraries
questions.explanation: Autologging records training details without explicit log calls.

questions.question: Which call opens a run for manual logging?
questions.explanation: mlflow.start_run() is usually used as a context manager around log_param, log_metric and log_artifact calls.

questions.question: What does an MLflow artifact typically hold?
options: Files such as plots, models and data samples
questions.explanation: Artifacts are files attached to a run, including the serialized model itself.

questions.question: What does Databricks AutoML produce besides the best model?
options: Editable notebooks for data exploration and every trial, plus a leaderboard
questions.explanation: AutoML is a glass box: every trial is a notebook you can read, edit and re-run.

questions.question: Why compare runs in the MLflow UI before choosing a model?
options: To weigh metrics, parameters and artifacts side by side on the same data
questions.explanation: The comparison view makes trade-offs visible before you commit a model to production.

questions.question: What does dbutils.data.summarize(df) show?
options: Summary statistics and distributions for each column
questions.explanation: It's a quick EDA view of nulls, distributions and basic statistics per column.

questions.question: What makes a Delta table usable as a feature table in Unity Catalog?
options: It must be in a Volume
questions.explanation: Any Delta table with a primary key constraint can act as a feature table.

questions.question: What does a point-in-time lookup prevent?
options: Label leakage from feature values recorded after the label's timestamp
questions.explanation: Joining features as of each label's timestamp keeps future information out of training.

questions.question: Which method builds a training set with feature lookups?
questions.explanation: FeatureEngineeringClient.create_training_set joins labels to feature tables using FeatureLookup definitions.

questions.question: When do you need features published for online serving?
options: For real-time inference with low-latency lookups
questions.explanation: Batch scoring can read the Delta feature table directly. Real-time endpoints need low-latency lookups.

questions.question: In Spark ML, what is a Transformer?
options: Something that fits on data and returns a model
Something that converts one DataFrame into another
questions.explanation: Transformers implement transform(). Estimators implement fit() and return a Transformer (the model).

questions.question: What does CrossValidator do?
options: Splits data into k folds and picks the parameter set with the best average metric
questions.explanation: It trains every parameter combination on k folds and keeps the best-scoring one.

questions.question: What does Databricks recommend for hyperparameter search now that Hyperopt is no longer shipped?
questions.explanation: Hyperopt left Databricks ML runtimes after 16.4 LTS ML. Optuna is the recommended replacement.

questions.question: Why use a model alias such as @champion?
options: Consumers load a stable name while you promote or roll back versions behind it
It is required to log a run
questions.explanation: Aliases decouple what callers load from specific version numbers.

questions.question: For churn, where missing a real churner is costly, which metric often matters more than accuracy?
questions.explanation: On imbalanced problems accuracy can look high while most churners are missed. Recall measures how many you catch.

questions.question: What are Foundation Model APIs?
options: Pay-per-token access to hosted models with no infrastructure to manage
A way to train models from scratch
questions.explanation: They serve open and proprietary models behind managed endpoints.

questions.question: Which table property must be enabled for an AI Search Delta Sync index?
questions.explanation: Delta Sync indexes read the Change Data Feed to stay in sync with the source table.

questions.question: Why chunk documents before indexing them?
options: So retrieval returns focused passages that fit in the prompt
questions.explanation: Smaller, coherent chunks improve relevance and keep the context window manageable.

questions.question: What are the three steps of a RAG chain in order?
questions.explanation: Retrieve relevant chunks, augment the prompt with them, then generate the answer.

questions.question: Why trace a RAG chain with MLflow?
options: To inspect retrieval and generation together and check whether answers are grounded
questions.explanation: A trace shows which chunks were retrieved and how the model used them.

questions.question: What makes an agent different from a fixed RAG chain?
options: The model decides which tools to call, and when, for each question
questions.explanation: An agent loop lets the model choose tools dynamically instead of always retrieving then generating.

questions.question: Which builder suits a low-code agent?
questions.explanation: Agent Bricks is the low-code option. The Mosaic AI Agent Framework is full-code.

questions.question: Why register an agent in Unity Catalog?
options: It becomes a governed, versioned object with access control like any other model
It removes the need for serving
questions.explanation: Registration brings versioning, lineage and permissions to agents.

questions.question: What is a DBU?
options: The Databricks Unit used to measure and bill compute
questions.explanation: Compute consumption is metered in DBUs, priced by compute type.

questions.question: Which change typically cuts cost for idle workloads?
options: Serverless compute or auto-terminating job clusters
questions.explanation: Paying only while work runs removes idle spend.
